newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo state kicks off power firms sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo state kicks off power firms sell-off.

text.p: Sao Paulo's state government kicked off its drive to privatize part of its power sector, issuing a preliminary tender document to hire consultants who will ready its three power firms for sale, officials said.

"It is going to be the world's largest privatization in 1997. Our three power companies have assets totalling $43 billion and a net worth of $23 billion," said Ricardo Lima, an official at the Sao Paulo state Energy Secretariat, who advises investors on the state's privatization.
Lima said the final version of the tender terms to hire consultants will be published by the end of the month.

One of the consultants will be responsible for doing a financial analysis and setting a minimum price for the sale. The second consultant will do this plus restructure the firm and design a privatization model, Lima added.
The preliminary tender document also contained the following points:
* Consulting firms will have 45 days after the final tender document is published at the end of the month to bid for the jobs.

* Winners will be chosen by the Sao Paulo state Privatization Council based on a score system, 70 percent of which will be determined by the proposal itself and 30 percent by the price the consultants charge.
* Winners will have 90 days to prepare their studies.
Lima said 115 investment groups, including J.P. Morgan and Brazilian Bozano Simonsen bank, have received copies of the preliminary tender document.

Under the preliminary document, each of the three power firms Eletropaulo, Cesp and Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz will have two different consultants who will determine a market value for the firms and design a model for their sale.

"It is the same strategy adopted by Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) for the privatization of federal firms because we want to be sure we will get the best appraisal for our firms," he added.
